blocks.text:
After breakfast, you set off to explore the famous Golden Circuit of Asunción! This tour takes you through the most iconic places in the city: the grand López Palace, home to the presidential offices and the seat of government; the National Pantheon of Heroes, with its solemn mausoleum and plaques honouring the great historical figures of Paraguay; and the House of Independence Museum, a colonial building that tells the story of how Paraguay broke free from Spanish rule back in 1811.

Lunch is enjoyed at Puerto Olivares Ranch, a lovely spot by the water. In the afternoon, you explore the nature trails of Puerto Olivares, surrounded by trees and wildlife. You return to your hotel in Asunción.

blocks.text: Paraguayan Chaco, Filadelfia and the Chaco War memorials

provenance.rationale: The website heading names the region, overnight stop and memorials described in the selected Word itinerary.

blocks.text: From Asunción, you'll drive about four hours to the Chaco, a vast region in north-western Paraguay. Here you'll find dry forests, hot plains, scattered settlements and dusty roads. Once you reach Filadelfia in the heart of the Chaco, you'll check in at your hotel. In the afternoon, you'll visit Fortín Toledo Reserve, where the local conservation centre works to protect the Chacoan peccary, known as the tagua. The Chaco is also home to armadillos, foxes, peccaries, anteaters and many birds. You'll then visit Chaco War memorials, including the fort, cemeteries for Paraguayan and Bolivian soldiers, and other sites that commemorate the conflict between Paraguay and Bolivia in the 1930s. The Chaco War has been described as the deadliest South American war of the 20th century.
